metadata.explanation: Task requires cloning the django/django repository to /home/user. Evaluator verifies the clone was successful by checking that the repository root contains at least 1 Python file (setup.py is a well-known file in Django repository). This is a simple check that confirms the repository structure is present.

llm_judge_reasons: Verification threshold too weak: Checking for only 1 Python file is insufficient to verify a successful git clone of the Django repository
Missing git repository verification: Does not check for .git directory existence or verify it's actually a git clone
Missing repository identity verification: Does not verify this is specifically the Django repository (could be any directory with a single .py file)
Incomplete clone detection gap: A partial, corrupted, or incomplete clone might still pass if it contains at least 1 .py file
Agent could trivially bypass: Creating a single dummy Python file would pass the test without actually cloning the repository
Expected value unrealistic: Django repository root contains many Python files (setup.py, setup.cfg related files, etc.), threshold of 1 is too permissive
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Increase minimum file count threshold to a more realistic value (e.g., >= 5 or >= 10 Python files at root level)
Add verification for .git directory existence: check if /home/user/django/.git exists
Add check for characteristic Django files like django/__init__.py or setup.py specifically (not just any .py file)
Consider verifying git remote URL matches 'https://github.com/django/django' using git config commands
Use recursive file count (remove -maxdepth 1) and check for minimum total Python files (e.g., >= 100) to ensure repository completeness
